<!-- generated by tools/gen_settings.py from the official proteus_f7 ini (config hash 1972639898); do not edit -->

| TunerStudio label | Setting | Units | Range | Help (as TunerStudio shows it) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enable Fuel Cutoff | `coastingFuelCutEnabled` | choice |  | Enable fuel cutoff in the selected Overrun, Decel or Both mode. Coolant, MAP, tuning and Lua guards apply to every mode. |
| Fuel cut on | `dfcoFuelCutMode` | choice |  | Overrun uses the TPS, RPM and vehicle-speed thresholds below. Decel requires Enable Engine State Machine and its Decelerating state, or RPM falling faster than the Decel RPM rate threshold when no vehicle-speed sensor is configured. Decel does not use the overrun TPS/RPM/speed/gear gates. Both accepts either path. Coolant, MAP, tuning and Lua guards apply in all modes. Active state-machine shifts suppress fuel cut. |
| No cut below CLT | `coastingFuelCutClt` | {bitStringValue(unitsLabels | {useMetricOnInterface ? 0 : 17.77777} … {useMetricOnInterface ? -100 : -148} | Fuel cutoff is disabled when the engine is cold. |
| Cut fuel below MAP | `coastingFuelCutMap` | {bitStringValue(pressureUnitsLabels | 0 … {useMetricOnInterface ? 0 : 0} | MAP value above which fuel injection is re-enabled. |
| Fuel cut delay | `dfcoDelay` | sec | 0 … 10 | Delay before cutting fuel. Set to 0 to cut immediately with no delay. May cause rumbles and pops out of your exhaust... |
| Inhibit closed loop fuel after cut | `noFuelTrimAfterDfcoTime` | sec | 0 … 10 | Pause closed loop fueling after deceleration fuel cut occurs. Set this to a little longer than however long is required for normal fueling behavior to resume after fuel cut. |
| Ignition retard during cut | `dfcoRetardDeg` | deg | 0 … 30 | Retard timing by this amount during DFCO. Smooths the transition back from fuel cut. After fuel is restored, ramp timing back in over the period specified. |
| After cut timing ramp-in time | `dfcoRetardRampInTime` | s | 0 … 1 | Smooths the transition back from fuel cut. After fuel is restored, ramp timing back in over the period specified. |
| Overrun RPM cut above | `coastingFuelCutRpmHigh` | rpm | 0 … 5000 | This sets the RPM above which fuel cut is active. |
| Overrun RPM restore below | `coastingFuelCutRpmLow` | rpm | 0 … 5000 | This sets the RPM below which fuel cut is deactivated, this prevents jerking or issues transitioning to idle |
| Overrun vehicle speed cut above | `coastingFuelCutVssHigh` | {bitStringValue(velocityUnitsLabels | 0 … {useMetricOnInterface ? 0 : 0} | Above this speed, allow DFCO. Use this to prevent jerkiness from fuel enable/disable in low gears. |
| Overrun vehicle speed restore below | `coastingFuelCutVssLow` | {bitStringValue(velocityUnitsLabels | 0 … {useMetricOnInterface ? 0 : 0} | Below this speed, disable DFCO. Use this to prevent jerkiness from fuel enable/disable in low gears. |
| Overrun TPS closed threshold | `coastingFuelCutTps` | % | 0 … 20 | Throttle position below which fuel cut is active. With an electronic throttle enabled, this checks against pedal position. |
| Overrun requires detected gear | `coastingFuelCutRequiresGear` | choice |  | Require a valid DetectedGear greater than zero for the Overrun path. Neutral, unknown or invalid gear prevents overrun fuel cut. Configure gear detection before enabling. Does not restrict the Decel path. |
| Enable Engine State Machine | `useEngineStateMachine` | choice |  | Classify engine operating state and recognize shifts. State-based STFT is separately enabled below. |
| Decel RPM rate threshold | `smDecelRateThreshold` | RPM/s | 0 … 10000 | Engine SM: RPM/s rate threshold to enter the Decelerating state (RPM falling faster than this). Also the accumulator normalizer in Overrun. 0 disables the Decelerating state. In VSS Rate mode this numeric value also normalizes the accumulator signal in km/h/s. |
| RPM rate averaging window | `smRpmRateWindowMs` | ms | 0 … 1000 | Engine SM: Time window used to compute RPM rate of change (RPM/s, "RPM/t") for Accelerating/Decelerating state detection and the RPM-rate shift-accumulator signal. Larger values smooth out sensor/tooth noise at the cost of slower response, smaller values track faster but are noisier. Internally floored to one slow-callback tick (50 ms). smAccelRateThreshold/smDecelRateThreshold stay in RPM/s regardless of this setting and do not need re-tuning when it changes. |
